findings.issue: Calling T the positive square root of Delta requires more than the self-adjoint field in D1a3OutputBGL. That interface does not require T positive or identify the supplied J with the polar conjugation of S.
findings.countermodel_mechanism: For any such T,J,S=JT, replacing T by -T gives S_new=-S, preserves self-adjointness, domain, closedness, involution, SdagS and its modular multiplier, but Fix(S_new)=i Fix(S). Thus those fields alone do not certify T=Delta^(1/2) or J as the canonical modular conjugation. This is an algebraic conditional sign ambiguity, not a claimed new Lean inhabitant.
findings.required_addendum: Require T nonnegative and prove T^2=Delta on the correct graph/domain, or construct T through the positive multiplier exp(sigma/2) after partial Fourier and prove its identification with the positive square root. Then identify J with the polar modular conjugation. No change to the already pinned type is needed for this contract addition.
